api: REST API, largely OpenAI-compatible, which makes swapping it in unusually easy. That ease is itself a shadow-IT risk worth naming.
cons: Hosted service sits under Chinese jurisdiction
Restricted on government devices in several jurisdictions
Content behaviour reflects Chinese regulatory requirements
name: DeepSeek
pros: Frontier-adjacent reasoning at very low cost
files: Standard text and code handling on the hosted service.
value: Reasoning performance close to the frontier at a fraction of the cost, with open-weight releases. The capability is real. The governance considerations are equally real and are the reason it needs its own policy decision rather than a default allow.
engine: DeepSeek's own models, with several released as open weights.
latency: Reasoning models trade latency for quality, as elsewhere in the category.
quality: Genuinely strong at mathematics and code reasoning. Outputs reflect Chinese regulatory content requirements on politically sensitive subjects, which is a factual property of the model rather than a criticism.
tagline: Frontier-class capability at very low cost, from a Chinese vendor, which is the whole governance story.
use_cases: High-volume reasoning workloads where per-token cost dominates
Self-hosting an open-weight reasoning model on controlled infrastructure
Benchmarking against incumbents to test whether premium pricing is justified
integrations: Hugging Face and standard self-hosting stacks
governance_note: Treat the hosted API and the open weights as two different decisions. The weights can be run on your own infrastructure with no data leaving; the hosted API sends prompts to servers under Chinese jurisdiction, which triggers cross-border transfer analysis, and in some sectors and government contexts an outright prohibition. Several jurisdictions have restricted it on government devices. See the China AI regulation and global AI laws pages in the reference library before approving either.
training_optout: The hosted service is operated from China and subject to Chinese law, including data access provisions. Self-hosting the open weights removes the data path entirely and is the only version most regulated organizations should consider.
